dedupe_keys.name: faa aviation safety information analysis and sharing asias public data

description: The Aviation Safety Information Analysis and Sharing (ASIAS) system is the Federal Aviation Administration's platform for the open exchange of aviation safety data. Its public data catalogue links several national databases: the FAA Accident/Incident Data System (AIDS), with records of general aviation and commercial air carrier incidents since 1978 gathered from incident reports on FAA Form 8020-5 (accidents come from the NTSB database); the Aircraft Registry of over 320,000 active US civil aircraft, updated in real time; NASA's Aviation Safety Reporting System of voluntary reports of unsafe occurrences; NTSB safety recommendations to the FAA with FAA responses; BTS carrier traffic statistics; and preliminary accident and incident notices for the past ten business days. The FAA's accident and incident data pages also link runway incursion data and research. Data are searchable free online, and as US government data they are unrestricted; aggregated copies, such as runway incursions from 2001 on figshare, circulate. Caveats: the portal notes delayed refreshes of some sources, incident reporting is incomplete, preliminary notices change, and accidents must be taken from NTSB. The data support historical event analysis, fragility and safety modelling of airports and airspace, together with the NTSB CAROL database.
